page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.48xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud instance powered by 192 dedicated physical ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at a frequency of 2.7 GHz. Operating under the AWS Nitro System hypervisor on an arm64 architecture, each core executes a single thread with 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 384.0 GB, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage consists of 11,400 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage. Networking capabilities include a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps without bundled complimentary IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional parallel processing and memory throughput. The instance scored in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, memory bandwidth for uncached reads reaching 907.71 GB/sec, software compilation in Geekbench with Clang, and static web serving throughput reaching 169.75 GB/sec. Database benchmarks demonstrated top-tier results with PassMark database operations and 362.69 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core CPU stress-ng tests, single-threaded compression, and small-model prompt processing scored in average to lower tiers.

The bundled high-capacity local NVMe storage combined with a high physical core count delivers strong qualitative cost efficiency for IOPS-heavy parallel applications by reducing reliance on external block storage. The main technical tradeoff lies in moderate single-threaded responsiveness relative to its high multi-core capacity. Recommended workloads include distributed database engines, in-memory caching clusters like Redis, high-throughput web serving, parallel build environments, and batch data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 192 dedicated physical ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores running at 2.7 GHz under the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. It integrates 384.0 GB of memory, 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks showcase top-tier capabilities in multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, memory bandwidth exceeding 900 GB/sec for uncached reads, and database operations reaching 362.69 million Redis SET ops/sec. While single-threaded processing falls into average performance tiers, the density of physical cores and direct-attached storage provide qualitative cost efficiency for scale-out parallel systems. Primary suitable workloads include distributed database clusters, Redis caching nodes, parallel CI/CD compilation pipelines, static web serving, and high-concurrency batch processing.
